Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity model and GPU runway for Endor Labs pilot

Hi Amina —

Great speaking yesterday. Attached is the first-pass capacity workbook for the Endor pilot (endor_capacity_model_v1.xlsx). I kept this intentionally conservative so we can iterate quickly once you confirm traffic shape.

High level ask from our side: can you confirm a couple of traffic numbers so we can finalize a recommended reserved slab to present to procurement? Specifically: peak RPS, weekday vs weekend delta, and percent of sessions that do multi-turn chat (>5 turns).

What we estimated so far (assumptions are in the spreadsheet):
- Model target: redwood-13b-q4_2 (quantized chat variant)
- Expected peak request RPS (customer-provided guess): 200 RPS
- Average generation length: 240 tokens per response
- Effective KV cache hit expected (chat warm cache) ~35%
- Baseline tokens/sec demand = peak RPS * avg tokens = 200 * 240 = 48,000 tokens/sec
- Redwood per-GPU steady-state throughput (q4_2, batched, warmed cache): ~6,000 tokens/sec/GPU (estimate)
- Raw GPUs = ceil(48,000 / 6,000) = 8 GPUs
- Recommended initial reserved slab = 12 GPUs (30% headroom for burst + maintenance)

Notes / open items:
- If your average tokens per response is higher (>=400) we need to re-run; likewise if peak RPS >250.
- We typically bake in a safety window for p95 latency SLOs (see SLO note in sheet).

If you can drop the traffic sample (endor_traffic_sample_q1.csv) or confirm the three numbers below I’ll lock the recommendation and hand off to infra for final sizing.

Thanks —
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Tessa —

Thanks for the deck — attaching a small sample and the clarified numbers you asked for. See inline below and attached: endor_traffic_sample_q1.csv.

Quick answers:
- Peak RPS (app-facing): 220 RPS during launches / open hours (we see bursts up to ~280 for short 3–5 minute windows)
- Typical weekday vs weekend: weekdays ~1.0x baseline, weekends ~0.6x
- Multi-turn chat (>5 turns): about 18% of sessions; most are 1–3 turns
- Average generation length: we measure ~210 tokens historically, but for the pilot we expect longer responses on some flows — plan for 300 tokens avg to be safe.

SLO: product wants p95 first-byte latency <= 300ms for conversational flows; can accept slower for batch/vectorization flows.

Procurement: they asked for an initial committed quantity to present to finance; we’re aiming to commit within the next two weeks if the numbers check out.

Let me know if you want additional granularity (per-region split, top endpoints by volume).

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 08:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity model and GPU runway for Endor Labs pilot (traffic confirmed)

Team — forwarding Endor's clarified profile (excerpt below). Amina confirmed peak 220 RPS, average tokens to plan for is 300, and p95 target 300ms. Procurement wants a committed slab in two weeks.

Customer excerpt: "Peak RPS 220 (short spikes up to 280), avg tokens ~300, multi-turn share ~18%"

Quick napkin math I ran (more detail in attached workbook):
- Peak token demand = peak RPS * avg tokens = 220 * 300 = 66,000 tokens/sec peak
- Effective tokens saved by KV cache: 35% hit => effective load = 66,000 * (1 - 0.35) = 42,900 tokens/sec
- Per-GPU throughput (redwood-13b-q4_2, warmed, continuous batching): conservative estimate 5,000 tokens/sec/GPU for p95 <=300ms at peak (we lower the number vs earlier because Endor's avg tokens are larger and spikes matter)
- Raw GPU count = ceil(42,900 / 5,000) = 9 GPUs
- Add operational headroom: +40% for burst windows, model warm-up, and maintenance => 9 * 1.4 = 12.6 => round up to 13 GPUs
- Recommend reserved slab: 16 GPUs (2x8 GPU slab or single 16 GPU reservation) to allow for fast autoscale, spare capacity, and room for a larger model variant if the pilot expands.

Other considerations / tradeoffs:
- If we can push the customer to the q4_0 profile (still quantized but slightly higher throughput) we could target 6,500 tokens/sec/GPU and drop recommended reserved GPUs to ~10 (plus headroom).
- If KV cache warms better than expected (50% hit) their effective tokens drop to ~33k and we get down to ~8 GPUs baseline, 11 with headroom.
- p95 latency is sensitive to batching window and tail latency from multi-turns; Stef, can we simulate a 280 RPS 3-min spike with current autoscale policy and see p95 impact?

Action items: 
- Ben: prepare a short note for procurement explaining the recommended commit (why 16 GPUs, how headroom maps to SLOs) and a monthly cost estimate. Use the price sheet in the workbook.
- Karthik / Stef: run a brief benchmark with redwood-13b-q4_2 and q4_0 using Endor-like payloads (avg length 300, 18% multi-turn) and capture tokens/sec @ p95 300ms. Record KV cache off/on profiles.
- Tessa: I’ll put together the one-pager with a conservative and optimistic slab (16 vs 11 GPUs) and include mitigations (canary, fallback to smaller model).

Thanks — please reply here with test ETA so we can lock procurement briefing next Wed.

Tessa
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2027 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity model and GPU runway for Endor Labs pilot (benchmarks + recommendation)

Looks good — ran a short synthetic with the infra harness this morning. Key results (summary):

Test profile: avg gen length 300 tokens, 18% multi-turn (KV cache warm simulated at 35% hit), synthetic spike to 280 RPS sustained for 3 minutes.
Benchmarks (per-GPU p95 <= 300ms):
- redwood-13b-q4_2: 5,200 tokens/sec/GPU (observed at target settings, batching 40ms)
- redwood-13b-q4_0: 6,700 tokens/sec/GPU (same batching)

Using the observed q4_2 number: effective load with 35% cache hit = 66,000 * 0.65 = 42,900 tokens/sec -> GPUs = ceil(42,900 / 5,200) = 9 GPUs -> with 40% headroom -> 13 GPUs.

Operational recommendation:
- Commit: 16 GPUs reserved (two 8-GPU slabs) for month 1. Rationale: 13 GPUs covers p95 SLO on peak spikes with buffer; 16 gives room for ops, fast canary, and to absorb short-term growth without immediate autoscale.
- Autoscale policy: keep burst pool at 20% of reserved slab (3 GPUs) configured as warm spare for <2s cold-start failure recovery.
- Fallback model: provide redwood-7b-quant fallback at 1/3 cost; configure automatic route for non-critical endpoints if p95 starts approaching 400ms.
- SLA note for procurement: we can guarantee throughput / latency for the committed slab (documented in canary runbooks) but require telemetry hooks (tracing headers) to be enabled on the Endor side.

Next steps: Ben to draft procurement note & monthly cost using 16 GPU commit; Stef to schedule a longer soak that simulates week-of-launch patterns (24h run) to validate steady-state thermal behavior.

ETA: longer soak can start Friday (48–72h) if Ben / Tessa confirm procurement timeline.

— Karthik
